questions.q: What is a reference architecture, as distinguished from a solution architecture?
options: A reusable, generalized template meant to be adapted — a solution architecture is one org's actual built implementation
A purely financial budgeting document
A finished, deployable system that requires no adaptation
The exact same thing as a solution architecture
questions.explain: Reference architectures are reusable templates; solution architectures are a specific organization's real, adapted build.

questions.q: In the hub-and-spoke pattern, how does metadata flow?
options: There is no catalog of any kind in this pattern
Metadata never leaves its originating platform
Every platform feeds metadata into a single central hub
Each platform only shares metadata directly with one other platform
questions.explain: Hub-and-spoke centralizes metadata collection: every platform (spoke) feeds into one central hub.

questions.q: What distinguishes the catalog-of-catalogs pattern from a mesh of catalogs?
options: Catalog-of-catalogs has a lightweight central index registering domain catalogs; a mesh has no central index at all
They are identical patterns with different names
Catalog-of-catalogs forbids any domain from having its own catalog
A mesh requires exactly one central catalog holding all data
questions.explain: Catalog-of-catalogs keeps a light central index; a mesh of catalogs relies entirely on shared standards with no central index.

questions.q: What real example does the lesson give of the hub-and-spoke pattern?
options: A fictional company invented for this lesson
Microsoft's published reference architecture for Purview
A pattern with no real-world adopters
Only a pattern used in academic papers, never in practice
questions.explain: The lesson cites Microsoft's own published Purview reference architecture as a real hub-and-spoke example.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend starting from a known reference-architecture pattern rather than a blank page?
options: Reference architectures are legally required by regulation
It guarantees zero implementation cost
It avoids re-solving problems (and re-making mistakes) other organizations have already worked through, and gives a shared vocabulary for the design
It removes the need to ever adapt the design to local platforms
questions.explain: The lesson's rationale is faster, more defensible design and shared vocabulary — not cost elimination or legal requirement.
